questions.question: How do you identify hazardous materials on a shipping paper?

options.text: List hazardous materials at the bottom.
List hazardous materials at the top.
Highlight hazardous materials in the same color as non-hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: List hazardous materials at the top.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous items must be clearly marked. You can list them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" before the description in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: How should containers of nitric acid be stacked?

options.text: No more than two containers high.
Load them on top of other products.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than two containers high.
questions.explanation: Nitric acid containers can be stacked, but only up to two containers high. Do not stack them on top of other products.

questions.question: What must a shipping paper generally include?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response phone number on hazardous materials shipping papers. There are some exceptions to this rule.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from a building?
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a building, bridge, tunnel, place where people gather, or an open fire.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy or electronic image of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the carrier accepts them. For hazardous waste, the period is three years.

questions.question: What should a driver check about the shipping paper?

options.text: It matches the markings and labels on packages.
All packages are labeled as poison.
It is not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping paper to the package markings and labels. Make sure the basic description on the paper matches what is marked and labeled on the packages.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how can hazardous materials be identified?

options.text: By listing them in red ink.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials on a shipping paper must be clearly identified. List them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" before the description.

questions.question: What must be in the vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle.

questions.question: What is a sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper is in a business that typically uses hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
Your last shipment was labeled hazardous.
The shipper is in a bad neighborhood.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper is in a business that typically uses hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
questions.explanation: A shipment may contain hazardous materials if the shipper is in a business that uses them. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, and pest control companies.

questions.question: What incident does NOT require notification to the National Response Center?
questions.explanation: Report incidents to the National Response Center if someone dies, is hospitalized, there is $50,000 or more in property damage, the public is evacuated, or a major transportation route closes for more than one hour. Also report fires, spills, or contamination with radiation, bacteria, or toxins. Report any situation the carrier considers serious.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, what is important to know?

options.text: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to nearby packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to nearby packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around each radioactive package and passes through nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: If hazardous materials catch fire while you are transporting them, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Keep driving to the fire department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need special training and equipment. Unless you have this training, let emergency personnel fight the fire.

questions.question: Which location is NOT acceptable for keeping hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door
In a pouch on the passenger's side door
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door
questions.explanation: While driving, shipping papers must be in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within the driver's reach. When the driver is outside the vehicle, papers should be on the driver's seat.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others about hazardous materials?

options.text: By placing HazMat placards on the truck
By putting flashing lights on the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: By placing HazMat placards on the truck
questions.explanation: Shippers must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on vehicles carrying certain hazardous materials. Shippers must provide placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, how may you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the road and waving your arms
By keeping the driver's side door open

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down with explosives, use reflective triangles or electric lights to warn other drivers. Do not use flares or other signals that could start a fire with flammable cargo.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, what should the floor liner be made of?
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight and the liner must be non-metallic or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals contain no iron.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?
questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of each trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: How should shipping papers be kept?

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: What is true about portable tanks?

options.text: They cannot be removed from a vehicle
They are not permanently attached to a vehicle
They are permanently attached to a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not permanently attached to a vehicle
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks stay on a vehicle at all times. Portable tanks are bulk packaging that are not permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, how should it be cleaned?

options.text: Let it air dry without washing

questions.explanation: Wash parts of a vehicle exposed to corrosive liquids thoroughly with water.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: The identification number for a hazardous material should appear:

options.text: On a bumper sticker on the vehicle.

questions.explanation: The material's ID number must appear on the shipping papers and on the packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other large containers.

questions.question: While driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in another place where you can reach them easily while wearing your seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: If transporting explosives:

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: For Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must follow a written route plan. Avoid areas with crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions that may apply.

questions.question: Placarded vehicles must carry fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: The engine area of a placarded vehicle must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: During a cargo fire, opening the trailer doors may cause the fire to expand because it:

options.text: Changes the temperature of the trailer.
Provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire brings oxygen into the area. This can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: If a product requires a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, you must use it when transporting:

options.text: More than 100 pounds of the product.
More than 50 pounds of the product.
The product in a leaking container.

questions.explanation: For materials that require it, you must display both the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the hazard class placard for any amount of the material, even small amounts.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids, unless the engine is needed to run a pump. Ground the tank before opening the fill hole and keep it grounded until after closing the fill hole.

questions.question: If a vehicle with Class 1 explosives is in a collision, the driver should:

options.text: Not warn others of the danger.
Keep the explosives inside the vehicle until after separating the vehicles.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating the vehicles.
questions.explanation: Warn others of the danger and keep bystanders away. Do not allow smoking or open fires near the vehicle. Before separating the vehicles, remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: A driver must take the HazMat knowledge test:
questions.explanation: You must pass the written HazMat knowledge test in English and pass a federal background check before every CDL renewal.
